elements.label: Figure 1.23
elements.description: Grouped bar chart titled 'Impact of changes in growth and inequality on poverty projections'. Y-axis: 'Difference in $3.20/day 2011PPP poverty rate (p.p)', scale 0.0 to 1.8 with gridlines at 0.3 intervals. Legend: 2021 (teal), 2022 (orange), 2023 (gray). Values are approximate readings (not printed on bars): Growth downgrade: 2021 ~0.5, 2022 ~0.5, 2023 ~0.3. 1% increase in inequality: 2021 ~0.2, 2022 ~0.4, 2023 ~0.4. 2% increase in inequality: 2021 ~0.5, 2022 ~0.9, 2023 ~1.0. Growth downgrade + 1% increase in Gini: 2021 ~0.7, 2022 ~0.8, 2023 ~0.6. Growth downgrade + 2% increase in Gini: 2021 ~1.0, 2022 ~1.4, 2023 ~1.5. Source: World Bank staff estimations using VHLSS, 2020. The pattern shows that inequality-driven scenarios raise projected poverty increasingly over time, with the combined growth downgrade and 2% Gini increase scenario showing the largest impact, especially for 2022 and 2023.
